narration_script: Headphones have only two speakers, yet a game can place footsteps behind you and above. The trick begins before either channel reaches your ears. A spatial audio engine treats each sound as an object with a position, then calculates how that direction should arrive at your left and right ears. Tiny timing, level and frequency differences come from the head and outer ear. Together, those direction -dependent cues form an HRTF. Turn the camera and the filters change. Each channel's waveform shifts while your brain interprets the pattern as a sound moving through space. Ears differ so one generic profile will not feel equally precise for everyone. Personalised profiles can improve the match where a system supports them. There are still only two channels at the end. The three -dimensional stage happens in the filtering and your brain finishes the render.
